findings.title: `PasswordField` password visibility toggle fails when `type="password"` is passed as a prop
findings.body: In `PasswordField`, `{...props}` is spread on `InputField` after `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}`. When a caller passes `type="password"` explicitly—as `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` does at line 176 (`<PasswordField type="password" ... />`)—the spread `props.type` overwrites the computed `type` attribute, so clicking the show/hide password eye button never switches the input to `type="text"`.

findings.title: Dismissing the modal on the backup codes step leaves parent 2FA state out of sync
findings.body: `handleEnable` (line 135) now transitions to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` instead of calling `onEnable()`, and `onEnable()` is only invoked when the user clicks the footer `Close` button (`backup-codes-close`, line 269). However, `Dialog` still uses `onOpenChange={onOpenChange}` directly. If the user dismisses the dialog at the `DisplayBackupCodes` step via the Esc key, clicking the backdrop, or the dialog header close icon, `onOpenChange` closes the modal without calling `onEnable()` or `resetState()`. Because 2FA has already been enabled on the server by `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/enable`, the parent settings UI remains in the "2FA disabled" state and reopening the modal starts at `DisplayBackupCodes`.

findings.title: Third-party IdP users with 2FA enabled cannot use backup codes to log in
findings.body: In `authorize`, lines 114–129 skip the `IdentityProvider.CAL` and password checks only when `!credentials.totpCode` is false (which is how `/auth/login?totp=...` works for Google/SAML users who have 2FA enabled). They do not check `credentials.backupCode`, and `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` (line 180) renders `ExternalTotpFooter` instead of `TwoFactorFooter` when `totpEmail` is set, hiding the "Lost access" button. As a result, a Google or SAML user with 2FA enabled has no way to use a backup code at login (and even if submitted, `authorize` would reject the request with `ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled`).

findings.title: `expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on a Promise instead of the switch state
findings.body: `page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()` returns a `Promise<boolean>` (and moreover, a Radix UI `Switch` renders a `<button role="switch" aria-checked="...">` rather than a checkbox input). Passing that Promise to synchronous `expect(...).toBeTruthy()` without `await` always passes because any Promise object is truthy, and the test never closes the new backup codes modal via `backup-codes-close` (so `onEnable` is never called in this test). Use `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch][data-state="checked"]')).toBeVisible()` after closing the backup codes step, as the second test does.
